headline: Dow Falls 739 Points as Nvidia-Led AI Sell-Off Deepens Before Earnings
subheadline: The Nasdaq lost 2.5% and the S&P 500 1.9% on Monday as Nvidia fell for a third straight day after Jensen Huang's resignation, and a new chip-export rule tightened the pressure on AI stocks.
body:
• US stocks closed sharply lower on Monday: the Dow fell 739.38 points (1.4%) to 51,608.17, the S&P 500 lost 1.9% to 7,416.59, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5% to 24,509.76.
  • Nvidia was again the market's heaviest weight, down 4.1% to $156.14 — its lowest close since July 1, 2025 — in its third straight decline since Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive.
  • A new Commerce Department rule restricting remote access to advanced US chips, aimed at closing a leasing route used by Chinese companies, added a policy driver to the leadership turmoil.
  • The next test arrives Tuesday after the close, when Nvidia reports quarterly results — its first earnings release since Huang's exit, with interim CEO Colette Kress addressing Wall Street.

Wall Street opened a pivotal week with its third straight loss. AI-linked stocks dragged the US market lower on Monday, led by Nvidia, as the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as the chipmaker's chief executive met a new US rule restricting China's access to advanced American computing power, the Associated Press reported.

The numbers

The S&P 500 shed 145.08 points to close at 7,416.59, a fall of 1.9%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 739.38 points, or 1.4%, to 51,608.17, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 626.52 points, or 2.5%, to 24,509.76. Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX, surged 19%, according to CNN. The losses broadened beyond technology as the session progressed, but AI-focused companies were by far the biggest weights on the market, the AP said.

Nvidia at the centre

Nvidia sank 4.1% and was again the heaviest weight on Wall Street. CNN put its close at $156.14, its lowest level since July 1, 2025, and noted the shares are down roughly 35% since a record high on October 6, erasing about $2 trillion in market value; the stock is coming off its worst week in 19 months, and a raft of analysts cut price targets last week. The AP, measuring from the eruption of the scandal around Huang, put Nvidia's market-value loss at $735 billion. Other chip and AI-infrastructure names fell with it: Broadcom dropped 3.9% and Advanced Micro Devices 5.6%, according to the AP, while CNN reported Intel down 7.1%, Alphabet down 3.85% and CoreWeave down 6.1%. As we examined last week, founder exits at Apple, Alphabet and Uber offer a mixed record for what happens to a company's stock and strategy after a defining chief executive departs.

"The market was already worried about this risk before what happened at Nvidia. Now the risk has become even more serious."

— Zhiwei Zhang, President and Chief Economist, Pinpoint Asset Management, via AP

The policy driver

The sell-off was not only about one company's leadership. On Monday the Trump administration issued new rules to restrict remote access to advanced US computing chips and servers, the AP reported; CNN described the Commerce Department rule as putting new curbs on US exports to data centres that provide significant volumes of computing to companies based in countries subject to US arms embargoes, such as China, Iran and Russia. That closes a route by which Chinese firms could lease Nvidia computing power through data centres in third countries, and it lands a day before Nvidia's earnings — the first since Huang's exit — raise the stakes further. Investors are also watching Anthropic's expected initial public offering later this week, which CNN described as targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion.

Bonds, oil and the wider picture

The recent swings have overshadowed a strong earnings season: the big companies in the S&P 500 are on track to deliver earnings per share for the summer quarter nearly 32% higher than a year earlier, according to FactSet figures cited by the AP — the third straight quarter of growth above 25%. In the bond market, the yield on the 10-year Treasury eased to 5.13% from 5.15% late Friday, and Brent crude fell 3.5% to $92.44 a barrel as oil prices yo-yoed amid uncertainty over the war with Iran.

What to watch next

Nvidia reports its quarterly results on Tuesday after the close, with interim CEO Colette Kress set to speak to Wall Street. Investors have become accustomed to Nvidia not only beating expectations but guiding well above them, the AP noted; against a leadership investigation, a board search and a new export rule, both the numbers and the guidance will be read as a verdict on the AI trade itself. Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's latest meeting, due Wednesday, are the week's other scheduled marker for interest-rate expectations.

key_takeaways: Dow fell 739 points, marking a 1.4% decline.
Nvidia's stock dropped 4.1%, its lowest since July 1, 2025.
New US rules restrict access to advanced chips for China.
Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX, surged 19%.
Nvidia's market value loss reached $735 billion since leadership turmoil.
